doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Jazz education institutionalized
summary: Learning in colleges changes the music; take the best of both worlds.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Has the music been affected by the fact that it’s become almost institutionalized, that mostly it’s taught in colleges now as opposed to kind of on the job training?

It definitely will change the nature of what that music is, how you learn it. I suppose that’s why I’m even more adamant, even having come from a college environment, but knowing deep in my heart that that’s not how you learn how to play. It’s really through experience so you have to take the best from both worlds is my advice to any students who are going through a music education whatever, a formal music education. But there’s something to be said for both those approaches and how you use it as a player, composer, whatever. Take everything you can but you have to do it.
